## Question 1 (Populations and Parameters)

a) Give a relatively simple example of a population you might want to study (in your own work) and a parameter of interest.{{< hp glyph="a" >}} Be sure to clearly define what the population is and what the parameter is in your answer.

b) Identify the population and parameter of interest in the following example:{{< hp glyph="a" >}} *I am studying the side-effects of a new drug that will be prescribed to older adults (aged 70+) with high blood pressure. I want to know how safe it is for anyone who might be prescribed this drug in the future. I recruit 10 older adults with high blood pressure to take a 50mg dose of the new drug and report on how many headaches they experience.*

## Question 2 (Statistical Inference)

a) In your own words,{{< hp glyph="a" >}} describe what "statistical inference" is and why it is so important in the social and behavioral sciences.

b) Why is the size of a sample important to statistical inference? {{< hp glyph="a" >}} Be specific in your answer.

## Question 3 (Standard Error of the Mean)

Use this information to answer the following questions.

> I am studying the side-effects of a new drug that will be prescribed to older adults (aged 70+) with high blood pressure. I want to know how safe it is for anyone who might be prescribed this drug in the future.
> 
> I recruit 10 older adults with high blood pressure to take a 50mg dose of the new drug and report on how many headaches they experience that day. Here are their responses: `0, 4, 2, 1, 1, 0, 1, 3, 1, 0`.

a) Use R to estimate the average number of headaches experienced in this population. Print it.

b) Use R to estimate the standard error of your answer to Q3a (assume an infinite population). Print it.

## Question 4 (Normal and $t$ Distributions)

a) If I want to contain the middle 80% of the density of a normal distribution, how many SDs do I need to move above and below the mean? Include your R code and output.

b) What are the main differences between the Normal distribution and the Student $t$ distribution?{{< hp glyph="a" >}} Why do we tend to use the latter when calculating confidence intervals?

## Question 5 (Confidence Intervals)

a) Use the data from Q3 to estimate a 95% confidence interval for the mean number of headaches.

b) Write one or more sentences to report (i.e., describe in text) and correctly interpret these estimates.
